Hey everyone,

I’m writing this because I’ve hit a wall and genuinely need perspective from people who have dug themselves out of a multi-year hole.

Throughout school, I was always sharp. I picked up concepts quickly, scored well without burning out, and had genuine intellectual curiosity. But over the past 4 to 5 years, my life completely derailed. It started gradually and ended up as a complete lifestyle collapse:

Inverted Sleep & Chronic Fatigue: My sleep schedule is inverted. I stay up late into the night and sleep through half the day. Even after 9–10 hours in bed, I wake up exhausted, heavy-headed, and groggy.

The Cheap Dopamine Loop: My entire waking life runs on autopilot. The moment I open my eyes, I reach for my phone. It’s a loop of endless reels/shorts, binge-watching shows, and gaming for hours. When boredom or low mood hits, I compulsively masturbate 2–3 times a day just for a quick distraction.

Severe Cognitive Decline: My working memory feels shot. I read a paragraph and forget the first sentence by the time I reach the period. I struggle with basic recall, feel detached, and experience constant brain fog. Sitting with zero stimulation for even five minutes triggers severe restlessness.

Now, I need to prepare seriously for a high-stakes competitive exam. Every time I sit down at my desk, the reality of the syllabus hits me. I try to force an 8-hour study session, last barely 20 minutes, get overwhelmed, and retreat straight back to games or reels to numb the anxiety.

I know my old brain is still in there somewhere, but my nervous system feels completely fried. I don't want quick hacks or toxic motivation; I need a realistic, sustainable way to rebuild my baseline.

For those who recovered from a multi-year slump:

How did you fix the physical brain fog first? Did you tackle sleep, diet, and physical health before attempting heavy study schedules?

How did you detox without crashing? Going cold-turkey on gaming, reels, and compulsive habits usually leads me to relapse within 48 hours due to boredom and anxiety. How did you taper or replace them?

How did you rebuild cognitive stamina? What did your study ramp-up look like during the first 2–4 weeks when your focus span was down to zero?

I appreciate any honest advice, harsh truths, or structured routines that actually worked for you. Thanks.
